items.title: There's no scientific evidence tying 5G networks to the coronavirus pandemic. Howe...
items.snippet_en: The claim that 5G mobile towers spread the coronavirus, leading to an increase in cases where 5G was installed, is a conspiracy theory with no scientific basis. These conspiracy theories led to arson attacks on 5G towers and harassment of telecom engineers in several countries.

items.title: No link between 5G and COVID-19, UN agency confirms | UN News
items.snippet_en: The claim that 5G mobile towers spread the coronavirus is a conspiracy theory with no scientific basis. The International Telecommunication Union (ITU), a UN agency, confirmed in April 2020 that 5G is not responsible for the spread of COVID-19, calling it a "hoax that has no technical basis."

items.title: 5G and coronavirus (COVID-19)
items.snippet_en: The claim that 5G mobile towers spread the coronavirus is a conspiracy theory with no scientific basis. The UK government has stated that viruses cannot travel via radio waves or mobile networks, and that COVID-19 has spread in countries without 5G.

items.title: DHS to advise telecom firms on preventing 5G cell tower attacks linked to coronavirus conspiracy theories - The Washington Post
items.snippet_en: Numerous scientific and governmental organizations have debunked the claim that 5G mobile towers spread the coronavirus. The World Health Organization (WHO) has stated that viruses cannot travel via radio waves or mobile networks. Experts explain that 5G technology uses electromagnetic fields, and it is physically impossible for these fields to transfer particles like viruses. There is also no scientific evidence to support the idea that 5G compromises the immune system. These conspiracy theories led to arson attacks on 5G towers and harassment of telecom engineers in several countries.
